resources.string: Rules highlight requests that need attention. You still approve every request.
These are the defaults every connection starts from.
Nothing is set, so connections that inherit compare nothing.
Nothing is compared by default, so every request that inherits from here is flagged for attention. Connections with their own overrides are unaffected.
A rule never approves, stops or filters a request. It only decides whether the request is flagged when you review it.
Global rules are the defaults. A connection either follows a section or replaces it outright — sections mix freely.
Daily limits are the exception: a global daily limit counts every connection and cannot be raised or removed locally.
Every request still needs your approval here, and the wallet asks again for anything it signs.

Each section either uses Global rules or replaces that whole section for this connection. A connection override never adds items to a global list. These rules approve nothing and refuse nothing; every request still needs your hand here and in your wallet.

These rules are your own note about what this agent is expected to ask for. They approve nothing and refuse nothing. You approve every request by hand here and again in your wallet, whether the rules match it or not.
No global rules saved yet. Inheriting a section therefore means no rule is configured there.
No connection overrides saved. Every section and per-request threshold inherits.
Nothing is checked. Every request from this connection is shown as under restrictions, with the reason that no rules are configured.
No global check is configured. Connections that inherit therefore get no rule from this document.
Nothing is checked any more. Saving removes this connection\'s rules.
Saving removes the global document. Connections that inherit then have no rule in those sections; their own overrides remain.
May ask for nothing at all.
At most %1$s of %2$s across all connections per day, counted from what went through this app.
Not checked: %1$s. A request that matches everything above still says nothing about these.
Allowed and under restrictions both need your hand on the wallet. Neither is an approval, and neither stops anything.
Only these actions may be asked for
Not checked. Any kind of action may be requested, and the review says the kind of action was not covered.
Checked. A kind of action that is not ticked is outside the rules.
Nothing is ticked, so every request is outside the rules. That is a rule, not a blank.
On. Anything not listed is flagged for attention.
Off on purpose. This is not compared, and the review says so.
On with an empty list, so nothing matches and every request is flagged.
Not checked. Any asset may move. The thresholds below still apply to the assets they name.
Checked. An asset that is not listed is outside the rules.
Nothing is listed, so no asset may move. That is a rule, not a blank.
No asset listed. Add one to set a threshold for it.
Most across all connections per day, in SOL
Most per request, in base units
Most across all connections per day, in base units
Additional most for this connection per day, in SOL
Additional most for this connection per day, in base units
No threshold. Blank is not a threshold of zero.
Type a plain number, such as 1.5. No sign, no exponent, no spaces and no commas.
Larger than the largest amount a transfer can carry, which is %1$s base units.
A threshold of zero is not a rule. To allow nothing, leave the asset off the list.
The daily threshold is below the per-request one, so the per-request one could never be reached.
This app cannot establish how many decimal places a mint has without a transaction that carries it, so a token\'s thresholds are typed in that mint\'s own base units.
Only these wallets may receive funds
Not checked. Funds may go anywhere, and the review says the recipient was not covered.
Connection override: no recipient check. This replaces any global recipient list.
Checked. A payment to a wallet that is not listed is outside the rules.
Nothing is listed, so no wallet may be paid. That is a rule, not a blank.
Write the wallet that owns the funds, never a token account. The phone works the owner out of the transaction itself.
Only these programs may be called
Not checked. The transaction may call anything, and the review says the programs were not covered.
Connection override: no program check. This replaces any global program list.
Checked. A transaction that calls a program which is not listed is outside the rules.
Nothing is listed, so no program may be called. That is a rule, not a blank.
Every program the transaction calls is checked, the compute budget program included.
Not a Solana address. An address is base58 for 32 bytes.
Daily limits set here count spending across every connection. A connection can add a tighter limit of its own, but cannot raise or remove this one.
Connection overrides reset. Inherited global rules are unchanged.
Global rules removed. Connection overrides are unchanged.
Could not save. The rules on this phone are unchanged.
What you changed here has not been saved.
Rules are stored for this connection and this app cannot read the file.
Rules are stored for this connection by a later version of this app. Showing them here would show fewer rules than were set.
The stored rules name something this version has no name for.
Every request from this connection is shown as under restrictions until this is settled. Starting over replaces what is stored, and nothing here can show you what you are replacing.

This changes the effective value for every connection that uses Global rules in an affected section. Connection overrides keep replacing their sections, and connection daily thresholds remain separate.
Uses the global value. If no global rule is configured, this visibly means no check is configured.
Replaces this whole section for this connection. Items are not added to the global list.
Connection override: no asset allowlist check. This replaces any global asset list; thresholds remain independent.
Fix the fields marked below to see an accurate effective summary.
Resetting returns every section and per-request threshold to inheritance and removes connection daily thresholds. It does not delete or disable any global rule.
A per-request threshold can inherit or be replaced independently of the asset allowlist. A connection daily threshold is additional; it never disables or replaces the global daily threshold.
This connection explicitly configures no per-request check for this asset. It does not affect either daily threshold.
Global daily threshold: %1$s. Source: %2$s. It is read-only here.
Connection daily threshold: %1$s. Source: %2$s. It is additional to the global threshold.
A local threshold names an asset that this connection\'s replacement asset list does not allow. Add the asset or remove the threshold.

Global rules are stored but this build cannot read them. They are not treated as absent, so inherited effective values cannot be shown. You can still edit this connection without replacing the global document.
Global rules are stored on this phone and this app cannot read the file.
Global rules were stored by a later version of this app. Showing them here would show fewer rules than were set.
The stored global rules name something this version has no name for.

Every inheriting connection is shown as under restrictions until this is settled. Starting over replaces the global document and can change every inheriting connection; no connection override is deleted.
No rules are set for this connection, so nothing was checked.
Rules are stored for this connection and this app cannot read them, so nothing was checked.
This kind of request is not on your list.
That asset is not on your list.
That recipient is not on your list.
The transaction calls a program that is not on your list.
More than your threshold for one request.
More than your threshold for a day, counting what this app has already moved today.
This app has no name for this kind of request, so your rule about actions could not be applied to it.
Which asset moves could not be established, so your rule about assets could not be applied.
The transaction does not establish who receives the funds, so your rule about recipients could not be applied.
The transaction could not be read, so the programs it calls are not all known.
The amount could not be read, so no threshold could be applied.
Today\'s total could not be read, so your threshold for a day could not be applied.
This phone could not account for the whole transaction. What the rest of it matched says nothing about the part that was not read.
